questions.q: Someone is willing to pay £{w} for a coat and pays £{p}. What is the consumer surplus, in £?
A demand curve starts at a price of £{t} and the market price is £{p}, with {q} units sold. What is consumer surplus, in £?
questions.why: The triangle has an area of ½ × (£{t} − £{p}) × {q} = £{answer}.

questions.q: On a diagram, producer surplus is the area:
options: Above the supply curve and below the price
Below the demand curve and above the price
questions.why: It's the gap between the price and what firms would have accepted.

questions.q: All of the consumer surplus lost to a monopolist is deadweight loss.
questions.why: Part is transferred to the firm. Only the triangle is lost to everyone.

questions.q: Deadweight loss from monopoly arises because:
options: Units that consumers value above their cost aren't made
The firm pays too much tax
questions.why: Restricting output removes those gains from trade.

questions.q: Explain how price discrimination can affect consumer and producer surplus.

ideas.label: Consumers who pay more lose surplus, which goes to the firm
Producer surplus rises, or some consumers gain by paying less

questions.model: Consumers charged a higher price lose consumer surplus, which is transferred to the firm, so producer surplus rises. Consumers charged less can gain.
questions.why: Ask who pays more, who pays less and where the surplus goes.

tests.answer: Consumers who pay more lose surplus and it is transferred to the firm, so producer surplus rises.
